QUOTE: By default, `ssl->MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(state)` becomes `ssl->private_state`, so code that touches a field directly fails to compile. ... `#define MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(member) member` ... "**Library sources** can write `ssl->state` or `conf->min_tls_version` directly." ... "**Everything else** (applications, other programs, downstream code) still gets `private_*` names."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer explains that defining the opt-out macro gives plain member names (library, test programs), while ordinary consumers of the public headers get the `private_` renamed members.
